soundness_flags.label: oeq:certified-uniform-inference
soundness_flags.one_line: “Covariance-region radius” and the diameter metric are undefined for the arbitrary regions Calpha, and no stated region-shrinkage condition makes the claimed quantitative convergence a determinate target.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:sharp-replacement-radius / ass:invariant-noise-interior
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The legal contamination converse is conditional on an interior invariant-noise covariance Omega being positive definite, rather than the full positive-semidefinite BACKSHIFT nuisance class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact replacement radius on the conditional class Omega in S++p; the unrestricted PSD-noise result is not claimed.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes invariant possibly nondiagonal noise and diagonal intervention covariance, defines the unit-diagonal cycle-product-normalized diagonalizer class, proves its all-honest uniqueness criterion, and gives an almost-sure continuous-amplitude corollary.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 61(7), 2013; author version arXiv:1111.7088v3 checked
source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 1 and equation (21) in the author version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The theorem characterizes essential exact non-unitary joint-diagonalizer uniqueness by strict profile-collinearity modulus, for a supplied complete diagonal family.
The paper iteratively retains non-outlier target matrices using a residual-distance threshold and explicitly reports no convergence proof for that outlier-aware procedure.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information Processing over Networks 6, 2020 author-hosted publication PDF
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: R-JDSEM treats sparse within-matrix outlier components through an elementwise robust joint-diagonalization formulation; its noiseless uniqueness theorem uses Kruskal-rank and prior-edge information, not whole-slab replacement.

The paper uses sparse mechanism-change probabilities and the Mechanism Shift Score to identify a DAG with high probability; it does not analyze BACKSHIFT covariance-slab replacement or affine occupancy.
The paper establishes generic identifiability conditions for sparse causal coefficients in an instrumental-variable model, distinct from sparse BACKSHIFT intervention-support geometry.

source_verification_receipts.version: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 43(2), 2022
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper supplies equivalent congruence-diagonalizability conditions and an SDP-plus-numerical algorithm for one Hermitian matrix collection, not a complete subset-consensus BACKSHIFT solver.

source_verification_receipts.version: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 30(3), 2008
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies exact joint-diagonalization uniqueness and sensitivity/perturbation analysis, rather than confidence inversion across changing candidate subsets.

The paper analyzes estimators, tests, and confidence sets under sporadic identification failure for smooth sample-average criterion models, not algebraic certificates for corrupted BACKSHIFT covariance families.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a norm, a simultaneous-region radius r_alpha, and the set diameter/Hausdorff metric, then state explicit coverage and r_alpha-to-zero conditions in the open-ended question.
Add the explicit fully active support construction attaining m=2c+3, together with its pairwise occupancy calculation, as a boundary corollary of the support-frontier proposition.
Replace the feasibility-oracle agenda with a terminating semialgebraic decision procedure, stated input format and complexity bound, or keep it clearly separated as a future computational project.
